summary: The focused object printing claim does not require harness maintenance. Every parser accepted object depth is below the new printing limit.

assessment.necessity_reason: The harness prints only trees returned by parsing. Parsing rejects arrays and objects at the same nesting threshold that the new object printer rejects, and both printing routes start at depth zero.

before.requirement: Print a parser produced object at every nesting depth accepted by parsing without failure solely due to depth.
before.reason: The complete old object printer has no depth rejection, and the harness passes its parsed tree to a printing route.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Parser dispatch constructs container values through the array and object parsers.
Object parsing rejects a container at the nesting limit.
Array parsing applies the same limit to mixed container nesting.

after.requirement: Print a parser produced object at every nesting depth accepted by parsing without failure solely due to depth.
after.reason: Parsing and printing start at depth zero and count each nested array or object. The new object guard therefore rejects only depths that parsing already rejects.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Parser dispatch routes every array and object value through the guarded container parsers.
Object parsing rejects the same depth threshold.
Array parsing counts mixed nesting against that threshold.
Array printing counts mixed container nesting with the same threshold.
Parsing initializes depth to zero before dispatch.
Unbuffered printing initializes depth to zero.
Buffered printing initializes depth to zero.

assessment.comparison_reason: The same old harness parses input and prints the resulting tree on both sides. The added object printer guard matches the existing parser limit, so the frozen behavior remains reachable.
